data.title: Boeing may be considering additional layoffs, union says after meeting
data.description:
Boeing (BA) management has left open the possibility that additional rounds of layoffs could be coming, according to the company's engineering and technicians union, following a routine meeting with the company's senior engineering managers to discuss workforce issues, The Seattle Times reported late Thursday.

Boeing (BA) announced plans earlier this month to ​cut 5% of its commercial airplanes division's ~50K employees through attrition ​and layoffs, saying it needed to moderate its planned production increases for its 737 MAX jet to allow its factories and suppliers time to stabilize operations and that it would notify impacted workers in December.

The Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace union said the meeting left unanswered questions about how many union members were likely to be affected, which rolescould be cut, and "whether this will be the only round of layoffs."

"The Boeing engineering managers said they had not yet determined those facts, which our committee found both surprising and frustrating," SPEEA said.

The company's engineering managers told the union at the meeting that affected workers would be notified on December 9 but said "Boeing didn't know" when asked if this was the only date for layoff notices, a union spokesperson reportedly told Reuters.

Boeing (BA) managers told ​union officials that "employment ​at all Boeing ⁠Commercial Airplanes sites is under review, but layoffs won't necessarily impact all sites," SEEPA said it told its ~17K members.

SPEEA also said it has an annual attrition rate of 4.9%, meaning "attrition alone will not meet the short-term need to reduce the workforce."

data.title: S&P 500 is near a bottom, but breadth still shows final low is not there yet – BTIG’s Krinsky
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) is nearing a tactical bottom around the 7,000 level, though market breadth suggests the final low has not yet been reached, according to Jonathan Krinsky, chief market technician at BTIG.

With the index pushing down 7,100, the top end of BTIG's targeted range, Krinsky invoked an old Japanese proverb, saying, "Tactically the downside is 80% full here."

He expects a short-term bottom should materialize in the next few days around the 7,000 level.

Short-term capitulation indicators are flashing, according to the strategist. The Daily Sentiment Index for the S&P 500 (SP500) closed at 10, the lowest level since the Liberation Day lows in April 2025, while the VIX (VIX) curve inverted by over 6 points, also the most since spring 2025.

Krinsky believes that from the S&P 500’s (SP500) 7,000 level, the market "could see a 4-5% recovery, which would take it back up towards the 200-day moving average” at 7,348.

However, this is not the final low, Krinsky warned, pointing to market breadth as the key reason.

Currently, 50% of S&P 500 (SP500) stocks remain above their 50-day moving averages, he noted.

"In the last 30 years, if we look at all S&P 500 pullbacks of 8% or more, the median reading of names above their 50-day MA is 11%," the strategist explained, adding that "it would be unprecedented to be putting in a final low here with half of the S&P 500 still above the 50-day MA.”

Apple's (AAPL) resilience near all-time highs also signals more downside ahead, according to Krinsky.

Looking at all S&P 500 (SP500) bottoms since 2015, the closest Apple (AAPL) was to a 52-week high was -11.8% in August 2024, with the median at -23% below 52-week highs.

"It would be unprecedented to make a final low with the world's biggest stock so close to an all-time high," he said.

The strategist continues to see downside risk ahead for Apple (AAPL), calling it "likely part of a bigger washout."

data.title: HIVE Digital and BitGo among financial stocks to join Russell Microcap; Strive and Sachem Capital to exit
data.description:
As part of its 2026 semi-annual reconstitution, FTSE Russell released preliminary additions and deletions for the Russell Microcap Indexes, with several notable financial stocks set to enter or exit after the U.S. market close on Dec. 11.

Financial sector stocks scheduled to be added to the Russell Microcap Index include HIVE Digital Technologies (NASDAQ:HIVE), BitGo Holdings (NYSE:BTGO), Robostrategy (NASDAQ:BOT), Private Bancorp of America (NASDAQ:PBAM), and West Coast Community Bancorp (NASDAQ:WCCB).

Financial stocks set to be removed from the Russell Microcap Index include Strive (NASDAQ:ASST), Sachem Capital (NYSE:SACH), Granite Point Mortgage Trust (NYSE:GPMT), Porch Group (NASDAQ:PRCH), and eHealth (NASDAQ:EHTH).

The newly reconstituted indexes will take effect after the U.S. market close on Dec. 11, 2026, following preliminary list updates scheduled for Nov. 20, Nov. 27, and Dec. 4.

data.title: Boxlight declines on Nasdaq delisting threat despite $7.5M financing progress
data.description:
• Boxlight (BOXL) announced on Friday that the SEC declared its Form S-1 registration statement effective, clearing a key condition for its financing plan.
  • The second tranche of its Series D financing would provide $2M, bringing total proceeds to $7.5M.
  • The company also expects to access an equity line of credit of up to $15M.
  • It plans to use the proceeds to reduce debt and support working capital.
  • Separately, Nasdaq issued a delisting determination after Boxlight failed to meet the $2.5M minimum stockholders' equity requirement.
  • The company plans to appeal the decision by November 25, allowing its shares to continue trading on Nasdaq while the appeal is pending.
  • Following the announcement, the stock crashed over 19% to $0.68.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Micron leads semiconductor and AI stocks down as SOX plunges 7%
data.description:
Semiconductor stocks fell hard during Friday market action, led by Micron Technology (MU) plunging 11%, and further evidenced by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) dropping 7%.

Micron sank despite its CEO indicating earlier this week that supply would be tighter in 2027 and 2028 than it was this year.

AMD (AMD) tumbled nearly 8%, Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) declined 6%, Marvell (MRVL) sank 8.5%, Nvidia (NVDA) dropped 6%, Arm (ARM) dove nearly 9%, and Broadcom (AVGO) decreased 8%.

Broadcom was hit by a report Friday morning that revealed Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) is cutting planned shipments of its Broadcom-designed AI chips for 2027 while increasing orders for chips designed by MediaTek.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq (COMP:IND) dipped 2.5% by late morning trading. The Nasdaq has declined 15% since October 6.

"The same rate pressure hurting semis today could ultimately help create the bottom," said BofA analyst Vivek Arya in a Friday investor report. "US cloud capex is running ~$1.2Tn annualized vs. ~$1.5tn+ expected in CY27. Holding spend near today's run-rate implies ~20% CY27 capex haircut (~30GW vs. ~40GW expected) and up to 35-40% downside to AI semi EPS. Higher rates raise WACC, weaken marginal project IRRs + make external financing more expensive, potentially forcing lower-return projects out of buildout. N-t capex reset would hurt, but could make the cycle healthier: less speculative capacity, more disciplined spending, an underwriteable earnings base."

BofA said they are waiting to see capital expenditure reductions before becoming more positive on the semiconductor and AI trade.

"Our historical work shows the SOX typically bottoms 2-6 mos. before fundas and subsequently rallies ~42% on avg. as est. cuts become understood," Arya added. "The signal we want is therefore not higher earnings ests. It is lower capex/EPS ests. that stop producing lower stock prices. Peak rates can establish the multiple floor; quantified capex and EPS cuts can establish the earnings floor … That, more than the eventual Fed cut or earnings trough, could mark the start of the next SOX upcycle."

Analog stocks were also falling on Friday. Texas Instruments (TXN) and Analog Devices (ADI) both sank 5%, Onsemi (ON) was down 5.3%, and STMicroelectronics (STM) slid 6.5%.

Neoclouds and networking stocks were also bleeding during Friday market action. Nebius (NBIS) plummeted nearly 10%, CoreWeave (CRWV) collapsed by 9.6%, and IREN (IREN) tumbled 11%. IREN was downgraded to Strong Sell from Hold this week by Seeking Alpha's Quant system.

Coherent (COHR) cratered by 11%, Lumentum (LITE) slumped nearly 10%, and Ciena (CIEN) fell about 9%.

data.title: Wall Street trades lower as the tech space remains under heavy pressure
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages were mostly lower on Friday, as a further tech selloff has put the main indices on track for their steepest weekly declines in over a year.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.1%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -1.2%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -2.3%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, six of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with consumer staples leading the way higher, while info tech has been the weakest area. 

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's (ANT) much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities. 

The latest declines followed a bruising Thursday session in which all three major indexes fell more than 2%, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) dropped 11 basis points to 4.64%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) shifted down 10 basis points to 4.94%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) moved down 7 basis points to 5.33%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Fair Isaac Corp. (FICO) advanced +6.5%, while shares of Sandisk (SNDK) dropped -13.8%.

data.title: Sandisk slides 14% amid broad memory sector weakness
data.description:
Flash-memory company Sandisk (SNDK) declined almost 14% on Friday. The stock traded at $81.31, down $13.08 on the day.

The move coincided with broad weakness across memory and storage peers. STX, WDC and MU each fell about 10%, while the XLK technology sector ETF lost almost 4% and the QQQ fund fell about 2%.

data.title: The Buckle rises 7% on Q3 earnings beat
data.description:
Casual apparel retailer The Buckle (BKE) gained just over 7% on Friday after reporting third-quarter earnings that topped consensus on the bottom line. The stock rose $3.09 to trade at $44.87 in morning action.

The company's earnings report showed GAAP EPS of $0.94, a $0.10 beat. Revenue of $329.2 million missed consensus by $7.95 million. Comparable-store sales grew 0.6%, while online sales declined 1.4% to $52.2 million.
